parakeet: Ask yourself, who benefits from a system where suffering makes you holy? Because this whole blood for blessing setup, it's not just spiritual, it's political. Renee Girard caught it out decades ago. Cultures use sacrifice not to save souls, but to stabilize power. You pick a scapegoat, spill their blood, and suddenly the crowd feels united, cleansed, and obedient. Now apply that to Christianity. Jesus dies, and instead of dismantling the sacrificial system, Christianity enshrines it, turns it into doctrine, and makes it sacred. They say his death ended the need for sacrifice, but then built an entire theology where you're still emotionally sacrificing every day, killing off doubt, killing off desire, killing off anything that doesn't look like submission, mortifying the deeds of the flesh. And let's not even get into the common language of financial sacrifice and seed sow. That's not redemption, that's psychological control. Sacrificial logic trains people to accept pain as divine. And when you do that, you will endure abuse, injustice, and silence, thinking it makes you closer to God, which just so happens to make you real easy to control. Redemptive suffering isn't love, it's conditioning. They told you love looked like sacrifice, that real faith meant pain, that God only drew close when you were broken. That's not love, that's conditioning. See, Marlene Wanel calls it religious trauma syndrome. It happens when people are taught that love must hurt, that loyalty means obedience, and that questioning is betrayal. And some of y'all, you still can't say no. Not because you believe, but because you were trained to equate pleasing God with self-denial. This doctrine of redemptive suffering, it teaches people to endure, not to heal.
